report.summary: The release changes how console reports are written and displayed.
keyChanges: Error entries are now sent to the regular output instead of the error output because the new routing step does not recognize the error marker it receives.
The previous asynchronous option was a boolean, but the updated writer recognizes the text value "async"; passing true now uses the default write behavior.
A clear request now calls the updated writer without its required options, which can stop the log entry from being displayed.
Reporter configuration now merges supplied options with defaults, so a custom output stream is used instead of being left nested and ignored.
Writing now selects the configured error stream for error output; previously, synchronous error writes used the regular output stream.
The previous tag-formatting and separate sync/async write methods were removed, but the supplied evidence does not show their replacement behavior.
Report output now supports normal writes, synchronous writes, and asynchronous writes that wait for a drain event when the stream signals backpressure.
Fancy reports now use configurable icons; plain log entries without a custom icon can receive the default icon, unlike before.
Badge color styling now uses the text-color style for the badge background slot, so verify that colored badges still have the intended background.
qaChecks: Verify an error entry is written to the error output and not the normal output.
Check that a log entry with a clear request clears the terminal and is then displayed without an error.
Confirm that with the previous asynchronous option set to true and a stream that signals backpressure, the write waits until the stream signals readiness.

Verify in a logging setup with a slow output stream that logging with the second argument set to true previously waited for the stream to drain but now returns without waiting, and confirm this change is intended.

Check a setup with separate standard-output and error-output streams by emitting an error entry; before this release it went to error output, and now it goes to standard output, so confirm the new destination is intended.

Confirm in the fancy reporter that a badge-style entry with a custom color previously showed that color behind the badge text but now applies it to the foreground, and verify the new appearance is intended.
Verify that logging a plain message such as “hello” used to show the literal text “4$s” instead of the message, and confirm that showing “hello” now is intended.
Verify that logs previously went to the default output when you configured a custom output stream, and confirm that they now go to the custom stream as intended.
Verify that an error logged with synchronous output used to appear with regular output, and confirm that it now appears with error output as intended.

Verify in the report output that setting the background to red styles two consecutive messages; before this release both were styled red, but now the second lookup returns the collection of cached colors instead, and confirm this change is intended.

Verify the fancy reporter with only an error icon configured and an info message: before this release the standard info icon appeared, so confirm that the new behavior—losing the info icon and potentially failing—is intended.
Verify a normal log with the output stream supplied directly in reporter options appears in that custom stream, not the default stream.
Check synchronous error output with distinct output and error streams; it should appear in the configured error stream, not the regular output stream.

Verify that an asynchronous write with write returning false stays pending until the stream emits drain, then completes; with mode omitted, confirm it uses the stream's normal write result, and with mode set to sync, confirm it writes through the stream's file descriptor.
Verify a plain log entry with no custom icon displays the default ❯ icon; previously plain log entries omitted icons.
Check an info entry with the reporter option icons set to {"info":"!"}; confirm the output uses ! as its icon.
Confirm a badge log with color red displays a red background behind its type; the new styling path supplies text-color styling for that background slot.
uncertainty: The removed tag formatting and separate synchronous/asynchronous write methods have no supplied replacement implementation, so the new output for colon-containing tags and the new async completion behavior cannot be determined.

The supplied changes contain no prior implementation for comparison, so there is no evidenced input that the old code handled differently; application navigation and affected user-facing surfaces were also not identified.

The badge code now supplies text-color styling where the format expects background styling, but the supplied context does not establish whether colored badge backgrounds are intended to remain visible.

report.summary: The release overhauls logging and console reporting, changing how messages are formatted, routed, and displayed.
keyChanges: Error logs now pass an error flag under a different option name than the writer checks, so verify error output is still separated from normal output.

Write behavior now uses mode values, while the previous interface accepted an asynchronous boolean; fancy clearing also calls the writer without the options its new signature requires, so verify these cases complete without errors.
Reporter options now merge with defaults, allowing supplied stream, error-stream, time-format, and format settings to override them; previously those options were not merged.
Log formatting now uses a default line template with date, type, tag, message, and additional details, and normal and error output are routed through the selected stream and write mode.
Console output now supports default writes, synchronous writes to a stream’s file descriptor, and asynchronous writes that wait for a drain event when a write returns false.
Message formatting now maps named fields such as date, type, tag, and message to positional placeholders and caches compiled formats.
Background-color lookup now caches results; on a repeated name, the cache-hit path returns the cache object rather than the resolved color.
Log entries without an explicit icon now fall back to the default icon instead of suppressing the icon; configured icons can also replace the built-in icons.
Badge color styling now uses the foreground color style rather than the previous background color style, changing the appearance of colored badges.
qaChecks: Verify an error-marked log is written to the configured error output and not the normal output.
Check a log sent with the previous asynchronous input true waits for a delayed stream drain and completes asynchronously.
Confirm a fancy-reporter log with clearing enabled clears the console and still emits the log without throwing.
Verify that logging an error with asynchronous mode disabled previously sent it to the error stream but now sends it to the regular output stream, and confirm the new result is intended.
Check a log written to a backpressured output with asynchronous mode set to true; previously it waited for the output to drain, but now it does not, and confirm the new result is intended.
Verify that a red badge previously had a red background but now shows red foreground coloring instead, and confirm the new result is intended.
Verify in the default log output that sending “hello” with the additional argument “world” used to show the literal “4$s” where the message belongs, and confirm the new output is intended.
Check a reporter configured with a custom output stream: before this release its log went to the default stream, and confirm routing it to the custom stream is intended.
Verify that asking the reporter to select a writer for a non-error asynchronous log used to return an asynchronous writer, and confirm that this operation is no longer available as intended.
Confirm that giving the reporter a record tagged “app:worker” used to return prepared output with “app - worker”, and that no longer being able to request prepared output is intended.
Verify that writing to a stream that returns false and later drains used to resolve the asynchronous write after the drain, and confirm that removing this operation is intended.
Check that sending “failure” through the reporter’s dedicated error-output operation used to write to the configured error stream, and confirm that this operation’s removal is intended.
Verify that asynchronously sending “failure” through the reporter used to return a promise for writing to the configured error stream, and confirm that removing this operation is intended.
Check that synchronously sending “failure” through the reporter used to write using the standard-output file descriptor, and confirm that removing this operation is intended.
Confirm that synchronously sending “hello” through the reporter used to write using the standard-output file descriptor, and that removing this operation is intended.

Verify in a screen that uses background colors by requesting red twice: before this release both requests returned a usable red formatter, but now the second returns the cache object, and confirm whether that result is intended.

Verify by sending enough output to a slow pipe or file stream in asynchronous mode to trigger backpressure: before this release the write returned immediately, but now it waits for the drain signal, and confirm that delay is intended.

Verify that an add-on which retrieves the reporter's built-in icon list still starts and logs correctly; before this release it could retrieve the list, so confirm that no longer providing it is intended.

Verify the reporter with only a custom error icon configured, then display an informational message; before this release it used the built-in informational icon, so confirm that the new result, including any failure, is intended.
Verify a plain log message with no explicitly supplied icon; before this release it appeared without an icon, so confirm that displaying the default icon now is intended.
Verify that a configured normal output stream receives a log when it differs from the default stream.
Check that an error log is sent to the configured error stream rather than the normal stream.
Confirm that a default-format log includes its date, type, tag, message, and additional details in that order.
Ensure an asynchronous write to a stream whose write call returns false completes after the stream emits drain.
Verify async mode with stream.write returning false and then emitting drain: the write completes after drain, with the message written once.
Check the default mode by omitting the mode when stream.write returns false: the write call returns that result immediately rather than waiting for drain.
Confirm sync mode writes the supplied data to the stream’s file descriptor.
Validate a format containing [%date$s][%type$-7s] %tag$s %message$s %additional$s with corresponding values: the output places each supplied value in its matching field.
Check two consecutive lookups of the same background-color name, such as red: both should provide the resolved background color rather than a cache object.
Verify a log entry with type log and no explicit icon shows the default icon; previously this case showed no icon.
Check a reporter configured with icons.error set to !: an error entry should show ! instead of the built-in error icon.
Confirm a badge entry with color red uses red foreground styling rather than the previous red background styling.
uncertainty: No application navigation or role details were supplied, and the intended compatibility for callers that still pass the previous asynchronous boolean is not documented.
The supplied evidence does not show the replacement stream helper’s completion behavior, so whether it preserves waiting for drain on a backpressured stream remains to be confirmed.

No previous implementation is supplied for these additions, so an input handled before this change but differently now cannot be identified; the background-color cache-hit result is evident, but no supplied dependency or application surface establishes where its effect would be visible.
The supplied context does not say whether changing badge color from background to foreground styling is intentional; confirm whether the new appearance is acceptable.
